acquisition.why: Neighbourhood Facebook-group pre-sales and paid social are inbound and legal. But the UK household market barely exists because collection is statutory and council-run. Only niche commercial or bulky-waste angles remain, and those are B2B and local.

onboarding.why: A Stripe pre-sale checkout and bin-delivery scheduling can be automated. Bin drop-off itself is physical.

delivery.why: Trucks, drivers, dump runs and breakdowns. This is purely physical work.

support.why: Missed pickups, bin damage and HOA or neighbour complaints need human dispatch decisions.

scores.R_why: UK household waste is a council statutory service, so the US model does not transfer. Commercial waste needs a waste carrier licence, a truck (£40k+ [E]), drivers, an operator licence and depot parking. That is impossible on £300 and 6-8 hours a week with a toddler.
scores.M_why: UK commercial waste is dominated by Biffa, Veolia and council trade services. Private residential subscriptions only exist for garden or bulky waste, and councils already offer those at low prices.
scores.one_line: A credible first-hand US story, but structurally non-viable in the UK and capital- and labour-heavy. Not agent-runnable.

acquisition.why: Facebook Marketplace or ads and UK trailer-hire listings are inbound and legal. Leads still need credit vetting by a human.

onboarding.why: Credit checks, deposits, insurance additions, O-licence checks and physical handover coordination need judgement.

delivery.why: Physical trailers at depots. The lessor maintains them, but handover, recovery and theft follow-up are physical.

billing.why: Weekly recurring card or direct-debit billing can be automated. Defaults and deposit disputes need a human.

support.why: Breakdowns, damage claims, theft (3-5% unreturned claimed) and late payers need active human handling.

scores.R_why: Needs a UK lessor willing to permit subleasing, plus commercial insurance at £4k+ [E], which exceeds the budget. Credit risk exposure is £15-25k per lost trailer. The UK haulage market is smaller and has established hire firms like TIP, Ryder UK and Fraikin. Hard to run in 6-8 hours a week.
scores.M_why: UK trailer and van hire is mature and consolidated. Serving poor-credit hauliers is a niche gap, but margins are thin at about 15% and depend on supplier goodwill.
scores.one_line: A clever arbitrage in the US. In the UK it is a credit- and theft-risk business with capital needs far above £300 and heavy human exception-handling.

acquisition.why: Relies on an existing public-company brand and customer base. A solo founder has no audience to leverage.

onboarding.why: Regulated finance and insurance onboarding needs KYC and compliance.

delivery.why: Brokering mortgages, insurance and services needs FCA authorisation and partner integrations, with no automated core.

billing.why: Commission and fee collection from partners can be automated once deals exist.

support.why: Financial-services complaints, FOS obligations and multi-vertical support need humans.

scores.R_why: A visionary, corporate-scale concept needing huge capital, FCA permissions and multi-sector partnerships. HM Land Registry already digitises title, so on-chain records add little in the UK.
scores.M_why: UK home portals (Rightmove, Zoopla, Habito-style brokers, Checkatrade) are entrenched. Blockchain home records have no proven demand.
scores.one_line: An unproven corporate moonshot with no claims or numbers. Irrelevant for a £300 agent-run UK test.

acquisition.why: Amazon UK, Shopify with paid social, and AI-generated ad tests are inbound and legal. Race-pack sampling partnerships with organisers are B2B and need some human deal-making. Platform-dependent on Meta and Amazon.

onboarding.why: Ecommerce checkout and subscription sign-up are self-serve.

delivery.why: Physical goods, but Amazon FBA or a 3PL can fulfil. Supplier sourcing, quality control and repackaging need oversight.

billing.why: Shopify or Stripe subscriptions and Amazon payouts are automated.

support.why: Agents can handle returns and FAQs. Product-safety complaints and claim queries need escalation.

scores.R_why: A cheap ad-validation test is possible within £300 [E], but inventory, packaging and compliance push beyond that. Pollution-filtration claims risk ASA/CAP breaches and possible MHRA medical-device classification. Mouth-taping safety claims are sensitive.
scores.M_why: Mouth tape (Hostage Tape, Myotape) and nasal products like Intake and Rhinomed are already marketed to athletes on Amazon. No moat, easily copied, and dependent on unproven efficacy.
scores.one_line: A low-capex DTC consumable that agents could largely run, but it is a hypothetical brainstorm with claim-regulation risk and an already-crowded category.

acquisition.why: Cold email to dental and aesthetic clinics trading as limited companies is legal. Many clinics are sole traders or partnerships, though, so they need consent or screening. Closing £2k+ retainers usually needs sales calls.

onboarding.why: Ad account access, offer design, GoHighLevel setup, and clinic-specific compliance review of ad copy.

delivery.why: Agents can run Meta ad creatives, GoHighLevel automations, AI booking follow-ups and local SEO with human QA. Results accountability is high.

billing.why: Retainers and pay-per-patient billing via Stripe. Lead-quality disputes need humans.

support.why: Clients expect reporting calls and performance conversations, and churn occurs when results dip.

scores.R_why: His technical skills suit GoHighLevel and ad automation, and the test costs little. But it needs ad-spend proof, sales calls and client management beyond 6-8 hours a week. Strict UK rules apply: GDC guidance for dental, and the ban on advertising prescription-only medicines like Botox.
scores.M_why: Dental and aesthetic lead-gen is one of the most saturated agency niches in the UK and US. AI-agency floods since 2024 have commoditised it, and many clinics have been burned by agencies.
scores.one_line: A legal B2B channel and partly automatable delivery, but a hyper-saturated, relationship-heavy agency niche backed only by second-hand or hypothetical figures.

acquisition.why: Content, paid social and community are inbound. But the model depends on hit films and multi-million ad budgets.

delivery.why: Film production and distribution need creatives, rights deals and theatrical logistics.

support.why: Agents can handle member support. Filmmaker relations and rights need humans.

scores.R_why: Needs tens of millions in capital, film-industry relationships and FCA-regulated crowdfunding. Completely mismatched to £300 and part-time hours.
scores.M_why: Angel Studios and Pure Flix/Great American dominate faith media. The UK values-based audience is small, and distribution is hit-driven.
scores.one_line: An impressive first-hand case of Angel Studios at scale, but a capital-intensive, hit-driven media company and not a solo agent-run test.

acquisition.why: Facebook and Nextdoor ads, local SEO and web chatbots are inbound and legal. The outbound texting used in the source is not PECR-compliant for individuals or sole traders in the UK. Property-manager outreach by email to limited companies is fine.

onboarding.why: Quoting from photos needs judgement (voids and foam under-estimation lose money), and the remote win rate is about 25%.

delivery.why: Physical work by subcontracted foam lifters. The owner must vet subs and manage quality.

billing.why: 50% deposit and balance via online invoicing can be automated.

support.why: Job overruns, sub no-shows and quality complaints need human arbitration.

scores.R_why: The sell-and-subcontract model is low-capex. But UK foam-lifting operators are few, and demand is far lower because there are fewer slab-on-grade settlement problems. Job risk lands on the founder. Coordination exceeds 6-8 hours a week, and a £300 ad test could only generate leads, not cover job risk.
scores.M_why: UK concrete-lifting is a tiny niche served by a few specialist firms (e.g. Uretek, Mainmark). There is limited residential demand to arbitrage.
scores.one_line: A neat lead-gen-plus-subcontract playbook, but UK demand and subcontractor supply are thin. The evidence is 90 days of self-reported results from one interview.

acquisition.why: Facebook video ads for free inspections are inbound and legal. Agents can handle creative and follow-up, but the model relies on commissioned in-home sales reps to close.

onboarding.why: In-person survey with thermal imaging and a sales appointment for each lead.

delivery.why: Physical installation by subcontractors, with a project manager overseeing quality.

billing.why: Deposits and invoicing can be automated. Consumer finance, and grant schemes in the UK, need compliance.

support.why: Install issues, warranty and sub disputes need a human project manager.

scores.R_why: The ducted HVAC and Aeroseal parts do not apply to most UK homes. A UK analogue would be loft insulation, ventilation or retrofit. Doing that well needs TrustMark/PAS 2035 accreditation for grant work, credit-broking authorisation for finance, and a sales team. Far beyond £300 and part-time hours.
scores.M_why: UK retrofit demand is real thanks to ECO4 and the Great British Insulation Scheme. But the market is crowded with installers and lead generators, and policy-dependent. Mis-selling scrutiny is high.
scores.one_line: A credible first-hand $1M+ US playbook, but sales-rep- and subcontractor-heavy, and the product mix mostly does not transfer to UK housing. Not agent-runnable.
